races.title: State Senate, District 10
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Benton Sawrey
cands.bio: Republican state senator for North Carolina Senate District 10 (Johnston County) since January 2023. He is an attorney and partner at the Smithfield and Raleigh law firm Narron Wenzel, P.A. He previously served on the Johnston Community College board of trustees.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Sawrey's stance on data centers or on homestead property taxes. We also found no record of his position on limits on investor or foreign land buying, or on H-1B visas. We found nothing on his record on red-flag laws or suppressors, and nothing on abortion beyond a 2016 campaign statement. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored was empty, so his specific bills on these topics could not be confirmed. The statements about his own actions come from his campaign website and are not independently verified. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for 2026, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. No news reporting or controversies about him were found in the pages available.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he was born and raised in Smithfield, and Wikipedia and Ballotpedia both say he is a native of Johnston County and attended Johnston County schools.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Practicing attorney (business transactions, real estate and estate litigation) and law firm partner; North Carolina state senator since 2023, with work on health-care and appropriations legislation; earlier a community college trustee.
qual.why: He has served in the legislature since 2023 and has a law career, which fits the high band for lawmaking and budget work. His board and committee seats are not counted.
qual.label: He has served in the legislature since 2023 and has a law career, which fits the high band for lawmaking and budget work. His board and committee seats are not counted.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he supported the Back the Blue Pay Act, a $200 million package for raises, step-pay adjustments and bonuses for law-enforcement officers and changes to line-of-duty death benefits, which it says passed the Senate unanimously. This is the campaign's own account.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he voted to expand North Carolina's opportunity scholarship program and supports school choice, including charter, private and homeschool options. This is the campaign's own account.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he champions state funds for conservation easements and farmland preservation and co-sponsored a law adding protections for voluntary agricultural districts. This is the campaign's own account.

pro-life.evidence: His 2016 campaign website said: "I am pro-life and believe that abortion should not be used as a form of birth control. I support pro-life protections for the mother and child."

second-amendment.evidence: His 2016 campaign website called the Second Amendment right "paramount" and said the state should be vigilant against actions and federal directives that over-regulate responsible gun owners.

workers-first.evidence: His 2016 campaign website said illegal immigration is taxing schools, roads and communities, and called for securing the borders, discouraging illegal immigration and encouraging legal immigration.

prio.label: Matches 6 of 6 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 6 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign site says he was born and raised in Smithfield, and Wikipedia and Ballotpedia both say he is a native of Johnston County and attended Johnston County schools.

cands.name: Pat LeGrand
cands.bio: Pat LeGrand is a retired information technology professional who worked for Bayer in Raleigh and Clayton, a facility that later became Grifols. She lives in Clayton, Johnston County. This was her first run for office, as the Democratic nominee for NC Senate District 10.

endorsements.text: Everytown for Gun Safety is listed by Ballotpedia as endorsing LeGrand in 2026.
Ballotpedia also lists several Sway voting groups and voter guides, including Fair Map Fight Club, Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress, NC GIRLIES and YALLvote.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Pat LeGrand was raised; sources give only that she was born in Nebraska and attended Arlington High School, with no city or state. She has held no prior public office, so there is no record of actions in office. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B, abortion, police pay and pensions, or school vouchers and teacher pay raises. Her campaign site says she supports investing in public schools and retaining teachers but gives no figures. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable named endorsements beyond those listed. The campaign site's 'Proudly Endorsed By' section showed no names in the text we could read.

local.label: Roots 55: She was born in Nebraska and moved from California to North Carolina in 1997 for a job, about 29 years before the 2026 election, and has made Johnston County her permanent home.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Long IT career (computer operations, analytical support, technical projects, database design, international training projects) at Bayer and then Grifols, from which she retired. No elected office or legislative, policy or budget work is documented. She describes involvement in voter engagement and volunteer outreach.
qual.why: Her work history is in a field unrelated to writing law and budgets, and she has no record of prior office, so she falls in the low range.
qual.label: Her work history is in a field unrelated to writing law and budgets, and she has no record of prior office, so she falls in the low range.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: She says Johnston County's growth must be managed responsibly with adequate roads, schools, water and sewer, and that she supports protecting farmland and giving agricultural communities a voice as development continues. She also says she supports attracting businesses and jobs to the county.

second-amendment.evidence: She says she respects the Second Amendment and the rights of responsible gun owners. She also supports practical measures to reduce gun violence and keep firearms from people who pose a danger to themselves or others. She does not name specific laws on her site.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: She was born in Nebraska and moved from California to North Carolina in 1997 for a job, about 29 years before the 2026 election, and has made Johnston County her permanent home.
